questions.explanation: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms. Both atoms contribute one electron to the shared pair, and the bond is the electrostatic attraction between the shared electrons and the nuclei.

questions.stem: How many covalent bonds does a hydrogen atom typically form?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has 1 electron and needs 1 more to fill its first shell (which holds 2 electrons). Therefore, it forms one covalent bond by sharing one pair of electrons.

questions.stem: In a molecule of water (H₂O), how many covalent bonds does the oxygen atom form?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has 6 outer electrons and needs 2 more to complete its outer shell. It forms 2 covalent bonds, one with each hydrogen atom.

questions.stem: What is a double covalent bond?

options.text: Two shared pairs of electrons between the same two atoms
A bond that is twice as long as a single bond
A bond formed by two different elements
Two bonds between different pairs of atoms

questions.explanation: A double covalent bond involves two shared pairs of electrons between the same two atoms. For example, O=O in oxygen gas has a double bond.

questions.stem: How many covalent bonds does a carbon atom typically form?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 outer electrons and needs 4 more to complete its outer shell. It forms 4 covalent bonds, which is why carbon can form such a wide variety of compounds.

questions.stem: In a dot-and-cross diagram for covalent bonding, what do the dots and crosses represent?

options.text: Outer shell electrons from each of the two different atoms

questions.explanation: In dot-and-cross diagrams, dots represent outer shell electrons from one atom and crosses represent outer shell electrons from the other atom. Where a dot and cross appear together, this shows a shared pair.

questions.stem: Nitrogen (N₂) has a triple bond between its two atoms. How many electrons are shared in total?
questions.explanation: A triple bond consists of three shared pairs of electrons. Each pair has 2 electrons, so 3 pairs means 6 electrons are shared in total.
